subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw support for config, channel/gateway credentials, and provider auth profiles?
rationale: The code paths are identifiable, but the permanent design changes key custody, startup behavior, migrations, recovery, rotation, and provider/channel auth compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
options.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with explicit migration, recovery, rotation, and upgrade tests across config, SQLite auth profiles, backups, and SecretRefs.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the supported mitigation
options.body: Document that transparent native encryption is out of scope for now and focus this tracker on audit guidance, SecretRef migration coverage, and plaintext-residue cleanup.

options.title: Stage a narrower hardening path
options.body: Land a smaller scoped step such as SQLite-auth-store sealing or keychain-backed SecretRef migration while keeping this issue open for the full at-rest strategy.

recommendation.title: Design native encrypted-at-rest storage
recommendation.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with explicit migration, recovery, rotation, and upgrade tests across config, SQLite auth profiles, backups, and SecretRefs.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent current-main and partial-design history on the inspected auth/security storage paths.
